clue.text: Totally revealed — just!

parts.note: a secret that is revealed is out in the open
just means fair or right, as in a just cause

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something was barely uncovered, only just shown in full.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and 'just!' make it read as 'only barely', but 'just' is a plain synonym for the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally and the answer are adverbs meaning completely, as in refusing a request flatly.

clue.text: A means of heating the new gaol is required

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The newly built prison needs a heating system.
explanation.walkthrough: GAOL is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuel made from petroleum, once used to heat homes and light streets.

clue.text: Yank accepting challenge gains regard

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for pulling holds the word for compete

parts.note: to yank is to pull or tow
to vie is to compete or challenge

explanation.surface: An American who takes up a challenge earns respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb meaning pull; 'gains' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at or consider it.

clue.text: Foray the fashionable way

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A raid carried out in the trendy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid or incursion into enemy territory; also an advance into a new area.

clue.text: A Scotsman not accustomed to plain living!

definitions.text: A Scotsman not accustomed to plain living!

parts.words: A Scotsman not accustomed to plain living
parts.note: plain living suggests a simple frugal life, but read literally it means living on a flat plain rather than in mountains

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is plain as a simple life versus plain as flat land; a man from the mountainous north of Scotland lives on high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the mountainous north of Scotland, who lives on high ground, not lowland flats.

clue.text: Make up about a hundred without delay

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for making amends goes round the number

parts.note: to make up for a wrong is to atone for it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An urge to make amends to around a hundred people immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Without delay and the answer are adverbial phrases meaning immediately.

clue.text: Old-fashioned dress few find boring

parts.note: tire is an archaic word for attire or dress
some means a few

explanation.surface: Antique clothing that hardly anyone finds dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' sits at the end as the definition; the surface reads few people find it boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring and the answer both mean dull or wearisome.

clue.text: A little difference about one's causing a hassle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for subtle distinction goes round the next piece

parts.note: a nuance is a slight or subtle difference
one's means one is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A small discrepancy is becoming a source of annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I (one) plus the 's; 'causing a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is an annoyance, something bothersome and irritating.

clue.text: Given the right name in consequence

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the word for name sits within the word for result

parts.note: an end is a result or consequence
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Someone granted a proper name as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To be granted a right or claim to something.

clue.text: Purchase money always available on time

parts.note: L stands for pound, the British currency unit, from Latin libra
ever means always, as in ever hopeful
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Advice about buying: the cash is there whenever you need it, provided you are punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but here it means a firm grip or mechanical advantage, the sense in 'get a purchase on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in the sense of grip or mechanical advantage is exactly what a lever supplies.

clue.text: Some upstart is to replace this designer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brash newcomer is set to take over from an established designer.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer is a creative worker who draws or paints, a kind of creative professional.

clue.text: Cleverly admitting change of name in cooperative fashion

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the adverb for skilfully takes the shuffled word inside it

parts.note: cleverly means skilfully or ably

indicators.note: change of says the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cleverly accepting a change of surname, all very obligingly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' turns NAME into MENA, which goes inside ABLY after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a cooperative fashion means acting willingly and compliantly, open to persuasion.

clue.text: Like many a worker's leaning

parts.note: as means like, as in 'do as I do'
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many
a worker ant is the commonest kind of ant, so ant can stand for worker

explanation.surface: Describing a habit or tendency shared by plenty of employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaning' looks like a tendency or bias, but it is the physical sense: tilted. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning here means tilted at an angle, sloping rather than upright.

clue.text: Column in favour of grant

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a cession is a grant or yielding of territory or rights

explanation.surface: A newspaper column that supports giving something away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests a newspaper piece, but it means a line of people or vehicles moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A column of people moving forward in a line, like marchers in a parade.

clue.text: Romance had to be fantastic for Hector's wife

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: The love story of a Trojan hero's wife must have been extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Iliad, Hector, the Trojan prince, is married to Andromache; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan prince Hector was married to this woman, mother of Astyanax.

clue.text: Spot-on article about a junior minister

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
C stands for circa, Latin for about
a curate is a junior clergyman, assisting a vicar

explanation.surface: A precise newspaper piece on a junior government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junior minister' sounds like government, but it is a minister of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on means exactly right, precise and correct.

clue.text: Crooked characters get on in a Greek tragedy

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of line, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Dishonest people prosper in a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' is a link: the letters of GET ON IN A are the characters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy by Sophocles about a daughter of Oedipus who buries her brother.

clue.text: Make notes about a bird which is fast-moving

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for vocalising goes round the bird

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: Writing down notes about a speedy bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests jotting things down, but it means sing; 'which is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing or zipping along quickly, rushing from place to place.

clue.text: The play's the thing wherein I'll catch the-of the king" Shakespeare (Hamlet)

definitions.text: The play's the thing wherein I'll catch the-of the king" Shakespeare (Hamlet)

parts.words: The play's the thing wherein I'll catch the-of the king" Shakespeare (Hamlet)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: supply the missing word from Hamlet's line at the end of Act 2, about the moral sense of Claudius

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet plans to stage a play mirroring his father's murder to provoke a reaction from King Claudius and so expose his guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Hamlet's line names the king's inner moral sense of right and wrong, which the play is meant to prick.

clue.text: Shower season

definitions.meaning: to shower something, as with bullets or questions, is to pelt it
to season food is to add spice

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to pelt someone with missiles, and to add spice from the grinder to food.

clue.text: Upset, so tend to get drunk

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or overturned, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone upset enough to go and get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated by drink or drugs.

clue.text: They reckon a churchman's to receive Her Majesty

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the churchman's letters surround the royal initials

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a churchman, so a churchman's gives A, DD and S
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A clergyman is due to welcome the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They reckon' looks like 'people think', but it means those who add up.
explanation.definitionFit: People who calculate sums, totting up figures.

clue.text: A Parisian is only half in agreement

parts.note: un is French for a, so a Parisian's way of saying 'a'

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of the word only

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is only partly in accord with the proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes ON from ONLY; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement or concord, as when people act together as one in harmony.

clue.text: A dessert may well be insisted upon

indicators.note: may well be suggests the letters could form something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone at dinner firmly demanding a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Insisted upon and the answer both mean declared or maintained forcefully.

clue.text: Publicity is about over for handsome young man

indicators.note: over says the word for concerning is placed ahead of the word is

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A press campaign is almost finished promoting a good-looking youth.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Adonis was a beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name means any handsome young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the beautiful youth of Greek myth loved by Aphrodite, a byword for male good looks.

clue.text: The underworld boss writes a note arranging share out

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
pens means writes
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A gangland chief drafts a memo arranging how the loot is divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but it is Dis, Roman ruler of the dead; 'arranging' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out is to distribute or hand out in portions.

clue.text: Oriental combine that's come to light

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
to merge is to combine

explanation.surface: An Eastern business group whose existence has just been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' looks like a noun, a business group, but it is the verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to light is to appear or come out into view.

clue.text: Trains do rattle underneath the arches!

indicators.note: rattle suggests being shaken up, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Railway noise rumbling beneath a viaduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underneath the Arches' is also a famous old British music-hall song about sleeping rough under railway arches.
explanation.definitionFit: This architectural term names the inner curved underside of an arch.
